selfCheck.singleWordOptions: 詞彙題 8 題＋綜合測驗 4 空＝48 個選項詞，全數回查 words.json
selfCheck.sentenceOptions: 閱讀 6 題＋篇章結構 4 題共 40 個句子選項。words.json 只收原形不收屈折形（need 有、needs 無），故未命中 token 再查原形：非虛詞 token 200 個，直接命中 189 個、屈折形 9 個（needs→need、volunteers→volunteer、visitors→visitor、longer→long、decided→decide、opened→open、vegetables→vegetable、looking→look、expected→expect），實際未收錄只有 easier（easy 的比較級，原形已收錄）與 caf（café 去重音符後的殘形）。

questions.stem: To visit the nature reserve, every visitor must ______ a permit at the local office before entering the area.
questions.explanation: obtain a permit（取得許可證）是固定用法，句意是進場前先「拿到」許可；retain（保留）指已持有後繼續保有，與 before entering 的時序不符；contain（包含）與 permit 沒有此搭配；attain（達成）通常搭配目標或水準，不與 a permit 連用。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：obtain ← attain / contain / retain（-tain 形近同詞性）

questions.stem: Students who move here from small towns soon learn to ______ to the long commute and the crowded buses at rush hour.
questions.explanation: learn to adapt to（學會適應）是 learn to do sth 的固定結構，後面接 to + 名詞片語 the long commute and the crowded buses；adopt（採用）、attempt（嘗試）、attract（吸引）代入後都不能直接接 to 這個介系詞，句子不成句。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：adapt ← adopt（形近）；attempt / attract 為同級動詞語意干擾

questions.stem: When the town budget is limited, the council must give ______ to repairing the old bridge rather than building a new park.
questions.explanation: give priority to（把…列為優先事項）是固定搭配，決定兩件公共工程先做哪一件；privilege（特權）、principle（原則）、principal（主要的／校長）代入後都不構成「優先處理某事」，其中 principal 作名詞是校長，與 repairing the old bridge 無關。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：priority / privilege / principle / principal（形近同詞性）

questions.stem: The city council decided to keep the new parking rule ______, so that both small shops and large stores could follow it easily.
questions.explanation: so that both small shops and large stores could follow it easily 表示規定要「適中」，故用 moderate（適度的）；modern（現代的）與 parking rule 的可行程度無關，moral（道德的）用於停車規定不自然，modest（謙遜的）只形容人、不形容規定。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：moderate ← operate / tolerate；modern / moral / modest 為同級形容詞形近干擾

questions.stem: The teacher refused to ______ the names of the students who had failed the test, saying that it would shame them.
questions.explanation: refuse to reveal the names（拒絕透露姓名）與 saying that it would shame them 的語意一致；replace（取代）不作用於姓名，reserve（保留／預訂）與 rescue（營救）也不會與 the names 構成「說或不說」的動作。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：reveal ← revive / repeat / rental；replace / reserve / rescue 為 re- 動詞群

questions.stem: Years of practice are needed to ______ the skill of playing the violin well enough to join an orchestra.
questions.explanation: acquire a skill（學得一項技能）符合 Years of practice are needed 的因果；advise（勸告）、admire（欽佩）、accuse（指控）放不進「靠練習獲得技能」的脈絡，代入後語意不成立。
questions.distractorSource: ad- 形近同長度動詞群語意干擾：advise / admire / accuse

questions.stem: After the storm broke the bridge, workers worked for months to ______ it to its former strength before the town reopened the road.
questions.explanation: restore it to its former strength（使它恢復到原來的強度）是 restore A to B 的固定結構；rescue（營救）對象是人或動物的性命，resort（訴諸／度假地）與 retire（退休、退役）代入後都不成句。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：restore ← resort / retire / retort（re- 形近同詞性）

questions.stem: The manager ______ that every machine must pass the safety check before it is started, even during the busy season.
questions.explanation: insist that + 子句（堅持主張）是固定句型，與 even during the busy season 顯示的強硬態度一致；assist（協助）、resist（反抗）後接名詞或動名詞，enlist（徵募）後接人，三者都不能直接接 that 子句。
questions.distractorSource: lookalikes：insist ← assist / consist / enlist（in- 形近同詞性）

questions.stem: Members may 1. any tool they need, from drills to sewing machines, at no extra cost.
questions.explanation: at no extra cost（不額外付費）決定了這個空是借來用而不付租金或購買費，故用 borrow；waste（浪費）、destroy（毀壞）與會員取用工具的行為相反，mend（修補）則是對已損壞物品的處理，與 any tool they need 不合。

questions.stem: What do corals receive in return from the small organisms inside their tissues?
questions.explanation: 第二段末句說珊瑚回報給共生夥伴的是 shelter and clean water（庇護與乾淨的水），與題幹的 in return 完全對應；A 把方向弄反（食物是夥伴提供的）、B 的骨架是珊瑚自己造的、D 的陽光是夥伴利用的，三者都不是珊瑚得到的回報。
questions.passage: Coral reefs are among the most colorful places in the ocean. They are built not by rocks but by tiny animals. Each coral polyp builds a hard skeleton, and over many years the skeletons of millions of polyps grow together into a reef. Living corals depend on small organisms inside their tissues. These partners use sunlight to make food, and they share part of it with the coral. In return, the coral provides shelter and clean water. When the water becomes too warm, however, the partners leave or die. Without their food supply, the corals turn white. This process, called bleaching, may kill the reef or leave it alive but weak. Scientists warn that a bleached reef can lose its color within a few weeks and may take decades to recover. Protecting reefs now therefore matters more than restoring them later.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the relationship between corals and the partners inside them?
option_texts: The partner needs the coral more than the coral needs the partner.
The partner and the coral need each other to survive.
The coral gets all of its energy from the partner.
The partner can build the hard skeleton of the reef.
questions.explanation: 文章明寫夥伴提供食物、珊瑚提供庇護與水，雙向交換可推知雙方互相需要；A 文中無依據、C 與 they share part of it（只分一部分）相衝突、D 與 Each coral polyp builds a hard skeleton 相衝突。

option_texts: How a tiny animal can build a colorful reef.

questions.stem: What may visitors need to pay for at a repair café?
questions.explanation: 第三段說志工不收工費，訪客 may donate a small amount for the cost of spare parts，因此可能要付的是零件費；工費、入會費與門票在文中都明說不存在。
questions.passage: A repair café is a small event, often held in a community hall, where people bring broken household objects and learn to fix them with help. A kettle that no longer heats, a lamp with a broken wire, or a jacket with a torn pocket can all be saved. Volunteers at such events are usually neighbors who enjoy working with their hands; they do not charge for the work, although visitors may donate a small amount for the cost of spare parts. The idea began in the Netherlands and has since spread to many countries. Supporters say the main gain is not money but knowledge. A visitor who learns to replace a switch may repair the next lamp alone, without anyone else. Critics point out that some objects are still cheaper to replace than to mend. Even so, most visitors leave with something working, and many return to a later event with a new problem and a little more confidence.

questions.stem: What does the writer mean by saying a visitor "may fix the next lamp alone"?
option_texts: Visitors often break an object by accident.
A professional repair service is no longer useful.
One lamp is easier to fix than any other thing.
The real value of the event is to learn a skill.
questions.explanation: 前一句 Supporters say the main gain is not money but knowledge 提示這句在說「學會技能」的好處：學會換開關之後，下次自己就能修；A 文中未提、B 文中只說某些物品換新比修便宜，無法推論專業服務無用、C 把單一例子擴大為通則。

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is best put in ❶ of the passage?
option_texts: The local people decided to build a community garden on the empty land.
The new garden opened in April, and the first fresh vegetables were ready to pick in June.
Looking back, the project has cost the town less money than people expected.
The old factory shut down three years ago, and the town had to decide what to do with the land.
questions.explanation: ❶ 是全篇起點，要交代工廠關閉的時間與「空地要怎麼處理」的難題，銜接前句 changed after a factory closed，故選 D；A 是決定、B 是成果、C 是回顧總結，都不能置於段首。
